territorial_scope.description: Applies to the public sector and to private persons who reside, are located or act in Spanish territory; several provisions apply only to the State administration.

summary.short: Spanish statute, in force the day after its publication in the BOE of 13 July 2022, prohibiting discrimination on listed grounds in employment, education, health, goods and services, housing and media. It creates an independent equality authority, sets administrative fines, and asks public administrations to minimise bias in algorithmic decision-making.
summary.long: Ley 15/2022 is a general anti-discrimination statute that applies to the public sector and to private persons acting in Spanish territory (art. 2). It defines direct and indirect discrimination, multiple and intersectional discrimination, harassment, retaliation and positive action (art. 6), and prohibits discriminatory treatment in employment and collective bargaining (arts. 9-11), education (art. 13), health care (art. 15), social services (art. 16), goods and services offered to the public (art. 17), housing (art. 20), venues (art. 21) and media and online services (art. 22). Article 23 asks public administrations to favour bias-minimisation, transparency and accountability mechanisms for algorithms used in public decision-making, including impact assessments. It creates the Autoridad Independiente para la Igualdad de Trato y la No Discriminación (arts. 40-45), which may mediate and bring legal actions. Administrative fines range from 300 to 500,000 euros across minor, serious and very serious infractions (arts. 47-48). Civil liability and a shifted burden of proof apply in discrimination cases (arts. 27, 30). Several provisions are declared basic State law or apply only to the State administration (Disposición final octava).
